correctness.rationale: Survival fixed points follow from Poisson generating functions and have a unique nonzero solution iff \(ab>1\) by strict scalar concavity. The nonstandard global \(F(u)=\log[-\log(1-u)/u]\) strict-convexity lemma is proven by explicit coefficient monotonicity, implying strictly concave inverse. Its Jensen and chord bounds yield exact strict risk endpoints, equality, and monotonicity; the subcritical matrix resolvent gives exact mean infections and AM–GM equality. The standalone verifier passed 1664 deterministic finite checks; those checks corroborate but do not replace proofs. All boundary cases and unattained limiting lower bound are handled.

originality.rationale: No matched result in the accessible search and full-text material gives the sharp fixed-Perron-root nonextinction interval, strict imbalance monotonicity, or the paired subcritical expected-progeny reversal. Existing general multitype threshold and Poisson equations supply the starting point but do not themselves imply the new optimization. Historical priority is provisional, particularly for older books and inaccessible zoonotic-branching literature.
residual_risks: Older general branching-process monographs and 20th-century extremal survival inequalities may contain a disguised equivalent; historical priority is not independently certified.
Full body and supplementary material of Singh, Schneider and Myers 2014 were inaccessible; the abstract alone cannot rule out a relevant coverage theorem.
Only the precise two-type cross-Poisson fixed-spectral-radius family is proved; no general matrix heterogeneity or policy recommendation follows.

value.rationale: The Perron reproduction threshold alone does not fix outbreak risk. This theorem determines the entire sharp feasible risk interval, optimizer, all equality cases and strict asymmetry direction for a natural two-group pathogen transmission class, plus the opposite subcritical expected-burden ordering. The two-objective contrast explains a substantive limit of threshold-only epidemiological comparisons. Although idealized and without fixed total contact budget, the exact nontrivial extremal boundary is a meaningful mathematical benchmark.
